title: Capitol dedication; Rankin's gigs and campus dances
summary: Thomas got three days off for the dedication. Bud Rankin got him good jobs paying $8 to $10, and he played dances for seniors and with Mr. Jefferies.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: You're talking about the dedication of the capitol?
Yeah. And, we go there. They finally gave us 3 days, they've gotten permission and we didn't skip classes to do this which is wonderful. Skip classes for 3 days is wonderful.
Normally you couldn't get off the campus?

You could get off the campus up to a certain time. See I'm under, see I'm a boy around 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. I say right about this time I'm 14 years old and you had to account for yourself. Tremendous idea because the parents send you there, therefore, people and the president are responsible and he's got to know. It was a wonderful idea. And Bud Rankin and his family, they were -- he was the one who was musical ... he had all the good jobs that ever came through there. And I think I was fortunate he liked me. Liked my little work, you know, after he heard me. He said, 'Well, you have no problems at all.' And I don't think I had a gig in Jeff City that was under $8 Sunday. I mean that was under $10. An $8 gig, I mean he apologized. Tremendous saxophonist. Melodic. He played things like Whispering, the melody things on the saxophone. And there were two girls that we appreciated very much. They played pianos piano. They're pai and did just tremendous things, you know. Now while we're doing these things if we have a session like we were going to have a session for people to march, this is -- let's see what you might call this, Stan -- a night for maybe the seniors to get together so we had a little band there.

We're playing dances now, you know. With Mr. Jefferies we played in the auditorium and he gave me a lot of good points. I'll never forget him as long as I live. And, of course, that was the marching thing, as you know. And, no matter what I had to say, I still marched with ... that we were marching. But, it was a good band. We had to march under the damnedest circumstances.
